name: Regime + persistent macro confirm arms slow momentum (multi-day regime, not a one-day blip)
rationale: THESIS: A one-day reading above the risk-on floor can be macro composite noise; what matters for a slow swing trade is that the regime has been risk-on for a SUSTAINED window. I require macro_regime>floor NOW and ALSO macro_regime>persist_floor as read persist_lookback days ago — i.e. the risk-on regime has held for days, not flickered. Only then do I arm a slow 30d-ish trend. This filters the whipsaw entries where the composite straddles its floor. macro_regime is BOUNDED so the lagged level read is a legitimate persistence check. DISCONFIRMER: run the SAME slow-momentum entry with ONLY the spot macro_regime>floor gate (drop the lagged persistence condition). If the spot-only gate reproduces the persistent-gate net-of-fee Sharpe, the multi-day persistence requirement carries no info and this is just a single-day level gate — falsified. The persistence condition must reduce whipsaw and add net edge over the spot-only gate. Holding across a persistent regime keeps taker churn low.
catalyst: Macro regime has held risk-on for several days (spot AND lagged read both above floor) while a slow trend is up — a sustained window arms slow momentum.
